name: Dreco

attributes.attribute: lake in County Mayo beside Nephin

sources: Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co., Ltd., 1906–1924, 15.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dreco is an Irish heroine in the mythological history of Ireland. She was a sorceress of the Fomorians, a people the Book of Invasions describes as monstrous. Dreco used a poison draught to kill twenty warriors who were sent against her. Irish place-name poetry records the exact site of that slaughter. It happened at Nephin, also called Nemthend, a mountain overlooking Lough Conn in County Mayo. The same poetry calls Dreco a bard as well as a magician. Her tale survives in the Metrical Dindshenchas, an Irish collection of place-name verse.
